sources: Monaghan, Patricia. The Encyclopedia of Celtic Mythology and Folklore. Checkmark Books, 2008.
text: The wasteland is a mythic motif in Celtic story. A king wounded in body or mind brings ruin to his land. The land grows barren and the people face famine. The blemished king sits at the center of this motif. The Grail legend carried the motif into famous literature. The Fisher King is the most famous figure. He took a wound in the thigh or the groin. The wound left him unable to rule. He fished in the barren lakes and bore the pain and exhaustion. In Irish story a bard made a satire to force the failed king off the throne. In the Arthurian tales knights sought the Grail to lift the endless winter.

okr.objective: The wasteland is a motif of a wounded king and a barren land.
key_results: A wounded king leaves the land barren and brings famine.
